'''Rachael Padman''' (born 1954) is an Australian [[physics]] lecturer at the [[University of Cambridge]] in England. From [[Melbourne]], Padman was a graduate in [[electrical engineering]] from [[Monash University]], Australia, and specialised in [[radio astronomy]]. After her doctoral research, she has made contributions to research in [[stellar evolution]] (the formation of stars). She is now mainly involved in administrative works in teaching. Padman is a member of the [[International Astronomical Union]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Rachael Padman|url=http://www.iau.org/administration/membership/individual/6177/|publisher=[[International Astronomical Union]]|accessdate=6 March 2014|date=18 May 2011|archive-date=10 March 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140310130817/http://www.iau.org/administration/membership/individual/6177/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

A [[trans woman]], Padman underwent [[Sex reassignment surgery (male-to-female)|gender-affirming surgery]] in 1982 when she was undertaking a PhD in [[astronomy]] at the [[University of Cambridge]].<ref name=guardian>{{cite web|title=A gender for success| url=https://www.theguardian.com/society/2004/aug/14/health.socialcare|website=The Guardian|publisher=Guardian News and Media Limited|accessdate=6 March 2014|date=14 August 2004}}</ref> In 1996, she was elected a Fellow of [[Newnham College, Cambridge|Newnham College]], one of three all-women colleges in the University of Cambridge at the time.<ref name=garner>{{cite web|last=Garner|first=Clare|title=Fellows divided over don who breached last bastion|url=https://www.independent.co.uk/news/fellows-divided-over-don-who-breached-last-bastion-1257781.html|website=The Independent|accessdate=7 March 2014|date=25 June 1997}}</ref><ref name=featherstone>{{cite book|editor-last=Featherstone|editor-first=Mike|title=Body Modification|date=2000|publisher=Sage|location=London|isbn=9780761967958|pages=219–220|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=EBs1PCbwF_0C|edition=1st publ.}}</ref> She received opposition from some people, who argued, unsuccessfully, that Padman should not be made a Fellow as she was [[Sex assignment|assigned male at birth]].<ref name=guardian/><ref>{{cite web|last=Reynolds|first=Flo|title=Arts history: Germaine Greer|url=http://www.concrete-online.co.uk/germaine-greer/|website=Concrete|accessdate=7 March 2014|date=19 February 2013|archive-date=7 March 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140307215701/http://www.concrete-online.co.uk/germaine-greer/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Early life and education==
Padman was born in [[Brisbane]], in 1954, and attended Gladstone High School in South Australia and then [[Melbourne High School (Victoria)|Melbourne High School]]. She was the school [[cadet]] captain and won the rifle-shooting prize for two consecutive years. She obtained a first degree in electrical engineering from [[Monash University]] in Australia. She joined research work on radio astronomy at the [[Commonwealth Scientific and Industrial Research Organisation]] Division of Radio Physics in Sydney, for two years.<ref>{{cite web|last=Legge|first=Kate|title=Sex changes a school of thought|url=http://www.theaustralian.com.au/news/features/sex-changes-a-school-of-thought/story-e6frg6z6-1226227729945|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111226045527/http://www.theaustralian.com.au/news/features/sex-changes-a-school-of-thought/story-e6frg6z6-1226227729945|url-status=dead|archive-date=26 December 2011|website=The Australian|accessdate=6 March 2014|date=26 December 2011}}</ref>

In her autobiographical essay, "Rachael's Story", she discussed her lifelong [[gender identity]] as female, and one motive behind going to England was a hope for an opportunity to address her gender issues.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://ai.eecs.umich.edu/people/conway/TSsuccesses/RachaelPadman.html|title=Rachael Padman's story|website=ai.eecs.umich.edu|access-date=2 May 2019}}</ref> In 1977, Padman settled in England to work for [[Doctor of Philosophy]] (PhD) in [[astronomy]] at an all-male [[St John's College, Cambridge]], and did research at the University of Cambridge's [[Cavendish Laboratory]]. Among the first things she did on arrival in Cambridge was to approach John Randall at [[Charing Cross Hospital]] in London, who prescribed [[oestrogen]]. In 1978, she [[Coming out|came out]] as [[transgender]], and started with her PhD supervisor, [[Richard Edwin Hills|Richard Hills]]. She said ''Rachael'' spontaneously came up as her name one morning; she initially thought about using ''Susan'' from a pupil from her primary school, before renouncing because there were already two Susans in her laboratory, including the secretary. 

In 1981, she began living as a woman in her everyday life, and she had gender-affirming surgery in October 1982.<ref name="guardian" />

She received her degree in 1982 for a [[doctoral thesis]] titled "Short-wavelength observations of interstellar molecules".<ref>{{cite web |last1=Padman |first1=R. |title=Short-wavelength observations of interstellar molecules. |url=https://ethos.bl.uk/OrderDetails.do?uin=uk.bl.ethos.331756 |website=E-Thesis Online Service |publisher=The British Library Board |access-date=24 July 2023 |date=1982 |archive-date=24 July 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230724105006/https://ethos.bl.uk/OrderDetails.do?uin=uk.bl.ethos.331756 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

==Career==
Following her PhD, Padman moved to the US where she was a [[Miller Fellow|Miller Research Fellow]] at the [[University of California, Berkeley]]. She returned to Cambridge in 1984.<ref>{{cite web|last=Zagria|title=Rachael Padman (1954– ) physicist|website=A Gender Variance Who's Who|date=24 October 2008|url=https://zagria.blogspot.com/2008/10/rachael-padman-1954-physicist.html#.XXsYWWZ7mHs}}</ref> At the Cavendish Laboratory, she was appointed Deputy Project Scientist for the [[James Clerk Maxwell Telescope]] in Hawaii in 1984. She led teams working on the development of the early instruments and wrote much of the early data acquisition and spectral line analysis software.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2014 |title=Spotlight on Prof. Rachael Padman |url=https://thematildaeffect.tumblr.com/post/90558645701/photo-provided-by-prof-padman-spotlight-on |access-date=2025-06-30 |website=The Matilda Effect}}</ref> She worked there for four years until she became a University Lecturer in the [[Cavendish Laboratory|Department of Physics, University of Cambridge]], in 1998. Since 2005, she has been primarily involved in the administration of teaching in the Department of Physics. She served on the University Council from 2009-2016 and was the Director of Education in School of Physical Sciences from 2008-2014.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-04-17 |title=Dr Rachael Padman {{!}} Cavendish Laboratory Department of Physics |url=https://www.phy.cam.ac.uk/profile/dr-rachael-padman/ |access-date=2025-06-30 |website=Cavendish Laboratory Department of Physics {{!}} |language=EN}}</ref> At Newnham, she is both teaching physics and serves as Director of Studies in Natural Sciences.<ref name=guardian/> Her research interests include millimetre wave optics and receiver systems, low-mass star formation, in particular jets and outflows from young stars, and spectral-line data reduction software.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-02-13 |title=Rachael Padman {{!}} Newnham College |url=https://newn.cam.ac.uk/person/rachael-padman |access-date=2025-06-30 |website=newn.cam.ac.uk |language=en}}</ref> 

She was publicly [[outed]] in the press in 1996, when Padman was elected Fellow of Newnham College. The college statutes allowed only female members in the institute. The Principal, Dr. [[Onora O'Neill]], knew that Padman had undergone a gender-affirming surgery. Feminist [[Germaine Greer]], who was a member of the college's governing body, strongly opposed the appointment, saying that Padman was a man and male.<ref name="guardian"/><ref name="garner"/><ref>{{cite web|last=Mistiaen|first=Veronique|title=Can Cambridge's All-women College Survive The Change?|url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/1997/08/24/can-cambridges-all-women-college-survive-the-change/|website=Chicago Tribune|access-date=7 March 2014|date=24 August 1997}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last=Baty|first=Phil|title=The essential guide to sexuality|url=http://www.timeshighereducation.co.uk/features/the-essential-guide-to-sexuality/103547.article|website=TimesHigherEducation|publisher=TSL Education Ltd.|accessdate=7 March 2014|date=21 July 1997}}</ref> Fellows, students, and staff of Cambridge University supported Padman, and she was admitted without further opposition.<ref name=garner/><ref name=featherstone/> Clare Longrigg published an article titled "A Sister with No Fellow Feeling" in the 25 June 1997 issue of ''[[The Guardian]]'' making charges on Padman and containing remarks attributed to Greer. The article was retracted on 19 March 1998 as information was found to be false, and the accusation made against Greer was considered groundless.<ref>{{cite web|title=When Germaine wants a job|website=The Guardian|accessdate=7 March 2014|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/19981201212018/http://www.pfc.org.uk/news/1997/gfolly02.htm|archivedate=1 December 1998|date=1997|url=http://www.pfc.org.uk/news/1997/gfolly02.htm|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Writer Watch: Germaine Greer|url=http://www.ljmaywatchwords.com/107744590|publisher=Watchwords|accessdate=6 March 2014|archive-date=17 November 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221117092027/http://www.ljmaywatchwords.com/107744590|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Padman was awarded the inaugural ''[[Gay Times]]'' Barbara Burford Award<ref>{{cite web|title=Gay Times Barbara Burford Award 2017 |url=https://www.gaytimes.com/honours/dr-rachael-padman-recipient-barbara-burford-gay-times-honour/|website=Gay Times|accessdate = 1 December 2025}}</ref> for excellence in STEM in 2017.
